corrected_proposal.description_long: On March 3, 2026, the UAE Ministry of Defence reported cumulative air-defense figures for attacks since Iranian attacks began. It said the country had dealt with 186 ballistic missiles, destroying 172; 13 fell into the sea and one landed in the UAE. Officials also reported 812 Iranian drones detected, 755 intercepted and 57 landing within the country, along with eight cruise missiles detected and destroyed. The statement said the attacks caused three fatalities, 68 minor injuries and limited damage to certain civilian facilities. These are figures attributed to UAE officials; they are not a count of attacks occurring on March 3 and were not independently audited in the supplied excerpt. Reuters's later March 9 cutoff cannot be used as a March 3 snapshot. The record's earlier Trump escalation framing is not established by the material: it does not show Trump directed the attacks or the UAE briefing. No target location is identified for each projectile, and any causal link to a Trump decision remains unverified. This is an internal account of the briefing, not a finding about Trump's role.

corrected_proposal.title: WBUR Interviewed Atlantic Editors About Their 50-Moment Trump Project
corrected_proposal.description_short: A January 2019 WBUR interview described The Atlantic’s 50-moment project and its focus on presidential norm-breaking.
corrected_proposal.description_medium: On January 14, 2019, WBUR interviewed Atlantic editors about “Unthinkable,” a special report surveying 50 moments from Donald Trump’s first two years. Editor Adrienne LaFrance described its frame as the “shattering of norms” in presidential communication and treatment of institutions. The interview supports that editorial framing, not a proposal for institutional redesign.
corrected_proposal.description_long: On January 14, 2019, WBUR published an interview with editors from The Atlantic about the magazine’s “Unthinkable” package on Donald Trump’s first two years in office. WBUR described a special report of 50 moments, and Atlantic editor Adrienne LaFrance said the project’s framing was a “shattering of norms” across Trump’s communication and approach to institutions. She said the team reviewed the first two years and narrowed hundreds of candidate moments to 50. The revised description identifies the project and attributes its interpretation to the editors. The supplied record’s claim that this was a continuing structural diagnosis leading readers from rebuttal toward institutional redesign is not supported by this interview. The source documents editorial framing and a curated list; it does not identify a specific constitutional reform, establish that Atlantic described a single ongoing pattern as structural, or measure institutional effects. The frozen date of March 4, 2026 does not match the cited 2019 material. This card dates the documented interview to January 14, 2019 and leaves the package’s exact initial publication date unspecified.
corrected_proposal.date_status: WBUR interview publication date; exact initial package launch date not established.

source_fact_map.fact: WBUR described The Atlantic’s report as a 50-moment package about Trump’s presidency.
source_fact_map.quote: what they describe as 50 extraordinary moments in an extraordinary presidency
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: Wherever you stand, it’s easy to agree that Donald Trump is anything but a “usual” president. Next Sunday will mark two years since President Trump’s inauguration. And so the reporters and editors at The Atlantic have put together a special report that tries to take stock of this presidency with a cool head and clear eyes. Thanks to them, we have a look at what they describe as 50 extraordinary moments in an extraordinary presidency.

source_fact_map.fact: Atlantic editor Adrienne LaFrance said the project framed Trump’s conduct as norm-shattering across communication and institutions and narrowed hundreds of candidate moments to 50.
source_fact_map.quote: The pattern is sort of within the framing, which is this shattering of norms
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: Adrienne LaFrance: “The pattern is sort of within the framing, which is this shattering of norms, and so we see that happening across all different kinds of behaviors both in how he communicates with the press and the way that he sees institutions — that’s a major one, just a disregard for institutional norms. It happens in sort of small ways and then very big ways, and so I think, day-to-day, it can be hard to attach a weight to whatever it is that has happened, but looking back over two years — I mean, we had a research team comb through every single day of the first two years of the presidency and we had, at first, hundreds of moments that we wanted to parse down from. We wound up with 50.”
